title: Simultaneous isolation of CD45 tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, tumor cells, and associated fibroblasts from murine breast tumor model by MACS
protocol: Cultivate 4T1 cells in RPMI 1640 medium with FBS and PSA in a T75 flask.
Rinse subconfluent 4T1 cells with 5 mL of Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS).
Add 3 mL of trypsin to the cells.
Incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Add 5 mL of complete RPMI medium to stop trypsin activity.
Collect cell suspension and count live cells with trypan blue.
Adjust cell suspension to a concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells/100 μL RPMI 1640 medium without FBS and PSA.
Inject the cell suspension subcutaneously into the mammary gland of BALB/c mice.
Shave the mouse before the procedure.
Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane.
Inject 100 μL of tumor cell suspension subcutaneously under the teat using a 1 mL syringe and 26G needle.
Dissect the mouse to recover the tumor growing in the mammary gland.
Cut the skin up to the diaphragm and then detach from the peritoneum and the skin.
Use a scalpel to cut around the tumor contour.
Monitor tumor growth for about 15 days.
Resect tumors when their volume reaches at least 250 mm³.
Ensure that the maximum tumor volume is between 800 and 1000 mm³ before necrosis or immune infiltrates become significant.
Dissociate the tumor after removal.
Anesthetize the mouse by inhalation with isoflurane (1.5%).
Cull the animal by cervical dislocation.
Make an incision in the abdomen and cut the skin down to the diaphragm.
Gently separate the skin from the peritoneum, preserving the fibrotic capsule surrounding the tumor.
Remove the tumor using a scalpel without disrupting the capsule over the tumor.
Weigh the tumor immediately after removal.
Reconstitute the Miltenyi « Tumor Kit Dissociation » buffer according to Table 3 instructions.
Prepare an enzyme mix for tumor digestion from the Miltenyi « Tumor Kit Dissociation » in RPMI medium without FBS and PSA as described in Table 4.
Cut the tumor into 1–2 mm pieces in a petri dish using a scalpel.
Transfer the tumor pieces into C-tubes.
Rinse the petri dish with 2.5 mL digestion mix and transfer to C-tube.
Close the lids of tubes and place them onto the GentleMax.
Ensure that the tumor suspension is at the cap.
Turn on the heater to allow the cell suspension to warm up to 37°C.
Start the digestion with the program “37C_m_TDK_2”.
Centrifuge the C-tubes for 7 min at 300 × g at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Resuspend the pellets in 1 mL of RPMI 1640 medium containing 10% FBS and 1% PSA.
Pass through a 70 μM Smart Strainers filter on a 50 mL falcon tube.
Rinse the C-tubes with 20 mL of complete RPMI 1640 medium.
Filter the suspension with prewashed 70 μM filters.
Centrifuge the C-tubes for 5 min at 300 × g at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Resuspend the pellets in 1 mL of complete RPMI 1640 medium.
Count the cell number in digested tissue sample.
Prepare cell suspension for counting by mixing 10 μL of cell suspension, 89 μL complete RPMI 1640 medium, and 1 μL DAPI.
Perform a control without DAPI to determine more precisely the DAPI negative population.
Calculate the number of total cells in the tumor cell suspension.
Divide the total cells into two parts: ¾ for sorting CD45+ TILs and CAFs (suspension #1).
Use ¼ of the suspension for tumor cell sorting (suspension #2).
Centrifuge the suspension #1 at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Re-suspend the pellet in 90 μL of autoMACS buffer.
Add 10 μL of CD45 (TIL) Microbeads.
Mix the cells and CD45 microbeads well.
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C in dark in the fridge.
Add autoMACS buffer to have a final volume of 500 μL.
Equilibrate Multi-24Column Bloc plate with 2 ml of autoMACS buffer.
Load the sample mixed with CD45 microbeads onto the multiMACS device.
Collect the unlabeled cells that exit the column as Fraction A.
Wash the column three times with 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Collect the outgoing fraction and pool with fraction A.
Keep the pooled fractions at 4°C or on ice.
Place the plate on the upper part of the elution machine for cell elution.
Load 1 mL of autoMACS buffer to elute the positive fraction as CD45+ cells in a fresh tube.
Centrifuge the CD45+ cells fraction at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of complete RPMI medium.
Maintain the cells at 4°C for further flow cytometry analysis.
If used for different applications, store the cells at −80°C.
Centrifuge the fraction A at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant with a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 80 μL of autoMACS buffer.
Add 20 μL of the “Non tumor-associated fibroblast” depletion cocktail.
Mix well and incubate for 15 min in dark at 4°C in the fridge.
Add buffer up to the final volume of 500 μL.
Place the Multi-24Column Bloc plate on the multiMACS separator.
Start the “DEPLETE” program on the multiMACS.
Equilibrate the columns with 2 mL of MACS buffer.
Load samples mixed with non CAFs depletion cocktail to the column.
Collect the outgoing fraction (Fraction B).
Wash the column three times with 1 mL of autoMACS buffer.
Collect the outgoing fraction and pool with fraction B.
Centrifuge fraction B at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 80 μL of autoMACS buffer.
Add 20 μL of CD90.2-labeled beads to label CAFs.
Mix well and incubate for 15 min in dark at 4°C in the fridge.
Add autoMACS buffer to reach a final volume of 500 μL.
Place the Multi-24Column Bloc plate on the multiMACS separator.
Start the “POSSEL” program on the multiMACS and follow the instructions.
Equilibrate the columns with 2 mL of autoMACS buffer.
Load samples mixed with CD90.2 microbeads to the column.
Wash the column three times with 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Place the plate with the columns on the upper part of the elution machine.
Elute the positive fraction with 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Centrifuge the CAFs cells-rich fraction at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of complete RPMI medium.
Keep at 4°C or on ice until further analysis.
Centrifuge cell suspension #2 (step 24b) at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 80 μL of buffer.
Add 20 μL of the “Non tumor cocktail depletion”.
Homogenize the well.
Incubate 15 min at 4°C in the fridge.
Adjust the volume to 500 μL with autoMACS buffer.
Place the Multi-24Column Bloc plate on the multiMACS separator.
Start the “DEPLETE” program on the multiMACS and follow the instructions.
Equilibrate the columns with 2 mL of MACS buffer.
Load samples mixed with non-tumor depletion cocktail to the column.
Collect the outgoing fraction C which contains the tumor cells.
Wash the column three times with 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Pool the collected fractions from washing steps with fraction C.
Centrifuge fraction C at 300 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of Dead Cell Removal Microbeads.
Prepare 1× Buffer from 20× Binding Buffer Stock containing in the kit “Dead cell removal” with sterile H2O.
Store the buffer at 4°C or on ice.
Equilibrate the column with 2 mL of the previously prepared buffer.
Load sample mixed with dead cell removal cocktail to the column.
Collect the outgoing fraction D which contains the live tumor cells.
Wash the column three times with 1 mL of binding buffer.
Collect the outgoing fraction and pool with the fraction D.
Stain tumor cells, CAFs, and CD45+ cells with a panel of antibodies.
Analyze stained cells by flow cytometer to confirm phenotypes.
Use a cytometry panel to check viability and purity of total tumor cell suspension and each purified fraction.
Centrifuge the samples in Eppendorf tubes collected at each step and sorted populations at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 150 μL of flow cytometry staining buffer (FSB).
Transfer to V-bottom 96-well plate.
Centrifuge the 96 well plate containing cells at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of antibody cocktail prepared in FSB.
Incubate the cells with antibody cocktail at room temperature (15°C–25°C) for 15 min.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard supernatant and wash with 150 μL of FSB per well.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 150 μL of FSB.
Prepare unstained controls for every fluorochrome-dye used in the panel.
Prepare single-stained controls for every fluorochrome-dye used in the panel.
Use total tumor cell suspension for anti-CD45, anti-CD31, anti-Podoplanin, anti-CD26 and anti-EpCAM antibodies.
For CD140a, CD140b, and FAPA markers, use compensation beads.
Mix stained and unstained tumor suspensions for the mortality dye.
Create a new experiment on the Cytoflex flow cytometer using CytExpert software.
Set PMT voltage or APD gain using unstained and single-stained cells or beads.
Prepare a compensation matrix using unstained and single-stained cells or beads.
Check FSC/SSC parameters to correctly identify all cell subsets.
Create a gating strategy as shown in Figure 8.
Load all samples for analysis.
Add 500 μl of Trizol® to CD45 TILs, CAFs, and tumor cell samples in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf.
Incubate the samples with Trizol® for at least 15 minutes to destroy cells.
Pause point: Freeze samples in Trizol® at -20°C or -80°C for long-term preservation.
Add 100 μL of chloroform to the Trizol®.
Vortex the samples vigorously.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Collect 250 μL of the upper phase in a new Eppendorf tube.
Add 250 μL of isopropanol to allow precipitation of RNA.
Homogenize the mixture and incubate it for 10 minutes at room temperature (15°C–25°C).
Centrifuge the RNAs for 15 minutes at 12,000 × g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant without losing the RNA pellet.
Fill the tube with 1 mL of 70% ethanol and vortex it vigorously.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 7,500 × g at 4°C.
Repeat steps involving 70% ethanol wash and centrifugation a second time.
Dry the RNAs at room temperature (15°C–25°C) for 1 hour until completely dry.
Recover the RNA pellets in 10 μL of ultra-pure water.
Measure the RNA concentration and purity with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Dilute the RNAs to a final concentration of 100 ng/μL.
Transform the RNAs into cDNA by reverse transcription using Mix 1.
Incubate at 65°C for 5 minutes.
Add the mixture presented in Table 7 to the thermocycler.
Run a program of 10 minutes at 25°C, followed by 50 minutes at 37°C, then 15 minutes at 70°C, and hold at 4°C indefinitely.
Pause point: cDNA can be stored at 4°C for few weeks or −20°C for long-term storage.
Dilute the cDNAs by adding 180 μL of ultra-pure water to the Eppendorf tube.
Prepare a mix as presented in Table 8 and add it to the qPCR reaction along with primers from the genes of interest presented in Table 9.

Perform the following qPCR program using the QuantStudio™ 3 Real-Time PCR equipment: Start with 10 minutes at 95°C, followed by 40 cycles of 15 seconds at 95°C and 1 minute at 60°C. Note: This program can also be run on other equipment such as AriaMx Real-Time PCR (qPCR) Instrument or CFX Opus 96 Real-Time PCR System.
